@prosopo/provider 5.19.3 — BENIGN
Sample SHA-256:
7db9a8761bbc20ed697687484c62204a2c6251819150d68abdef7c588ac319ee

Identification and release comparison

Prosopo's Node.js CAPTCHA provider exposes Express challenge, verification,
administration, and bot-detection services. Both ESM and CommonJS entrypoints
export these services. No install lifecycle hook is declared. Production
entrypoints do not import the shipped regression tests.

Fetched the preceding release from:
https://registry.npmjs.org/@prosopo/provider/-/provider-5.19.2.tgz
Registry metadata: https://registry.npmjs.org/@prosopo%2fprovider
Both archives match their registry SHA-512 integrity fields. This establishes
byte agreement with the registry, not independent publisher authentication.

The unpacked release diff contains 25 changed paths and no added/deleted paths.
Three production modules change: handler.js, frictionlessTasks.js, ipMatch.js,
with corresponding CJS output, declarations/maps, and tests. Changes apply
verified Web Bot Auth Allow/Block policies before CAPTCHA shortcuts, invalidate
conflicting cached challenges, normalize IPv4-mapped IPv6 for session binding,
cap stale-payload puzzle escalation, and persist puzzle difficulty. Remaining
changes are dependency versions, changelog, and build logs. Scripts are equal.

The decisive credential match is at line 20 of:
dist/tests/unit/api/domainMiddlewareErrorBody.unit.test.js
Its SHA-256 in BOTH releases is:
95826c7e29849afba0de06f8e750f1b8185ee4ae0e9569d074f7ec0452b73023

Execution trace: vi.mock replaces Tasks with a database stub; the URL constant
is placed in errmsg on a mocked rejected getClientRecord call. The test sends
a POST to its own ephemeral 127.0.0.1 Express server, checks status 401, and
asserts that the returned text excludes the dummy password. The middleware's
non-API error branch logs internally and sends only generic Unauthorized text.
No MongoDB connection consumes this URL. Renaming the test to index.js retains
these facts, so the correction does not rely on a test filename or package name.

domainMiddleware.js itself is also byte-identical across the releases:
a5b3e11381c1ffb0bb253ca5a272b1b5c9833064018f57b8cf256733a2eae8f5

Obfuscation and intended behavior

Inspected the entrypoint graph, changed execution paths, and obfuscated decoder
modules, in addition to atomscan findings and cleave facts/strings. The three
decodePayload/decodeSimd/decodeBehavior files and the 827 KB browser detector
fixture are byte-identical to 5.19.2. The browser fixture hash is:
d3234e8446fe9b1df741dfcd9d4c1dc16cfe2013e603797ff643e6b5413f8846

Independently decoded decodePayload's custom 91-character alphabet and indexed
string table in Python, without executing the specimen. Recovered indices
0x8c..0x95 are parse, base64, sha256, aes-256-gcm, setAuthTag, update, concat,
final, toString, utf8; 0x97..0x9b name env, BOT_DECRYPTION_KEY, base64, toString,
ascii. The R_BPTt5 function parses key/data/iv, unwraps the key using the
imported RSA-OAEP privateDecrypt, sets the GCM tag, decrypts, and decodes text.
The exported decoder parses the result into score, timestamp, userId,
userAgent, WebView/iframe state, head hash, and detector signals.

Caller chain: frictionlessTasks.decryptPayload resolves the session bundle's
key/layout, calls getBotScore, and passes data through decoderPool. The worker
source imports three fixed local decoder URLs, dispatches a selected decoder,
and posts its result to the parent. getBotScore sanitizes reported detector
data before returning it for session storage and access-rule evaluation.
The generated Function('return this') fallback recovers the global object;
it does not evaluate an acquired payload. These operations fit anti-bot
processing. Existing Base91, crypto imports, computed-call, and generation
observations remain. No rule suppression was added for obfuscation or crypto.

Rule correction and consumers

The old published-mongodb-credential composite required only a published npm
manifest and a credential-shaped URL anywhere in that archive. Neither proves
credential harvesting, a live secret, or a security-boundary crossing. Its
T1552.001 mapping was unsupported. Move the same matcher and effective scope
to micro-behaviors/data/db/mongodb::packaged-credentialed-mongodb-url, notable,
described as a package containing a credential-shaped URL. The underlying
credentialed-mongodb-url matcher and all its exclusions are unchanged.

Audited exact references and ancestor selectors before moving. No exact or
api-harvest/token-directory consumer references the old rule. Four broad
credential-access selectors occur in Feishu/Slack and MCP-injection composites.
A URL's publication must not supply their acquisition/theft leg. Other source
legs remain. No MongoDB/data/db/data/property ancestor selector gains counting
or proximity evidence from the relocated observation.

Existing controls outside this batch retain exactly the same trait ID/severity
sets: version-drift-package-credentials/upload.js (actual credential-file to
HTTP-body transfer), cleanup.js, mongodb-synthetic-placeholder/live-shaped-url.py,
and synthetic-url.py. Four added archive controls retain runtime-shaped URLs,
reject documented placeholders, preserve the actual redaction test even under
index.js, and retain suspicious credential-transfer detection beside the URL.
Run python3 testdata/provider-version-drift/check.py for the focused checks.
They are also registered in testdata/expectations.toml for make validate.

Scan comparison and limits

Ran atomscan on the supplied archive before/after, with machine-readable slow
scans and dependency following disabled for a stable artifact comparison.
Both analyzed 1,132 units, including archive members and decoded units.
Exactly one finding changes: the archive-level suspicious objective becomes
the notable package URL observation. Every member-level ID/severity is retained.
Totals: suspicious 1 -> 0, notable 5344 -> 5345, baseline 5212 -> 5212,
component 1583 -> 1583. No supported attack detection was lost in these checks.

Classifier v18.18 / engine 2.13.0: generic raw probability 0.84596956 ->
0.8733346; npm route 0.006149888 -> 0.005595187; calibrated level remains -1
and route class remains 0. The explicit tiny scan says:
scan benign confidence=0.873
The elevated generic raw score remains a model-level discrepancy with the
source evidence, not a reason to preserve the misplaced objective.

The newly fetched 5.19.2 ALSO fires the old objective under the current rules;
the queue's earlier clean result cannot be reproduced. Both earlier and current
artifacts contain the same test URL. Analysis records source-flow budget gaps;
the verdict rests on inspected control/data flow and the release diff, not on
absence of findings. No real deployment configuration or server activity was
provided, and no live credential or database was probed. The balance of evidence
supports ordinary CAPTCHA maintenance and a dummy error-redaction test.
